data.body:
this should start the #demo channel

we'll need to build a deck-type demo. we're presenting this at a hackathon

build a react live interactive slide deck

the core demo slide will be a 1 minute timelapse through particle being created in our own UX from issue #1 to present. it should have creative ways to show off work being done by multiple agents and humans who prompted them

the demo should subtitle things happening

the judging rules:

-Technical Difficulty (30%) – Did you tackle a challenging engineering problem?
-Execution (25%) – Does your project work? Is it polished and well-built?
-Creativity (20%) – Is your idea original or a novel approach to a problem?
-Impact (15%) – Does your project solve a meaningful problem or have real-world potential?
-Presentation (10%) – Can you clearly communicate what you built and why it matters?

And finally: everything scores extra for being something someone would actually use.

the judges will presumably be affiliated with yc so it's important to make sure to show off the actual user impact and need

we created this because we needed it internally - important (and actually true)
